advances:
This breaks the coalesced-side restriction in accepted fact
`16b9eb59c6ee0306`.  The two sides joining the singleton vertices of
the \(Q\)-triangle to its triple vertex now have independent rational
slopes.  Their coordinate-line crossings are allowed to separate,
subject only to the exact ordering that prevents the forbidden
\(Q_{13}\) and \(Q_{23}\) cells.  The larger empty cell remains a
separator-normal trapezoid.

All four positive \(Q\)-cell areas, both actual-lower-crossing
derivatives, the area of
\(C=\operatorname{conv}(\overline{Q_1}\cup\overline{Q_2})\), and the
polygonal support formula for \(V(P,C)\) are computed exactly.  The
old contradiction persists with a different sharp mechanism.  Either
one of the first two actual crossings gives
\[
 \frac pm<\frac{2}{sR}<2,
\]
whereas accepted fact `904839a1c6967954` gives
\(p/m>\beta>2\).  Hence this full two-slope class is empty before
either mixed-area gate is tested.  No general mixed-area lower bound
outside this class is asserted.

proof:
Equations (3)--(6) follow exactly as in the common affine
normalization of accepted fact `16b9eb59c6ee0306`:
\[
 f_i+L_i
 =\Delta r_i+2L_i
 =-(\Delta+2)\tau_i.
\tag{24}
\]
The linear part of (6) is \(-sI\), so every \(\tau\)-area is
multiplied by \(s^2\) in the common \(r\)-area normalization.

We first determine the exact sign cells of (11).  On the side
\([y_1,y_3]\), the parameters from \(y_1\) at which
\(\tau_2\) and \(\tau_3\) vanish are
\[
 t_2=\frac{\rho}{\rho+y},
 \qquad
 t_3=\frac{\omega}{\omega+z}.
\]
The first inequality in (8) is exactly \(t_2\leq t_3\).  Thus this
side passes from \(Q_1\) into \(Q_{12}\) no later than it reaches the
\(\tau_3=0\) line.  It never enters \(Q_{13}\).  Similarly, on
\([y_2,y_3]\), the second inequality in (8) says that
\(\tau_1\) vanishes no later than \(\tau_3\), so that side never enters
\(Q_{23}\).

The part of the triangle with \(\tau_3\geq0\) is bounded by the two
side points at which \(\tau_3=0\) and by \(y_3\).  At both side
points the other two coordinates are nonnegative by the
ordering just proved.  Convexity therefore puts this whole upper
triangle in \(Q_{123}\).  Below \(\tau_3=0\), the base segment
\([y_1,y_2]\) contains a nondegenerate interval on which
\(\tau_1,\tau_2>0\).  A relative neighborhood of that interval lies
in \(Q_{12}\).  The two remaining corner regions are \(Q_1,Q_2\).
This proves the exact support (13), including positivity of all four
listed cells and absence of every other cell.

We now compute their areas in \((\tau_1,\tau_2)\)-coordinates.  The
base \([y_1,y_2]\) lies on \(\tau_3=-\omega\) and has vector
\((-R,R)\).  Its affine height from \(y_3\) is \(H=\omega+z\).
Therefore
\[
 |A_2|_\tau=\frac{RH}{2}.
\tag{25}
\]

The line \(\tau_2=0\) cuts the base at
\((1+\omega,0,-\omega)\) and the side \([y_1,y_3]\) at
\[
 b_1=(1+\varepsilon_1,0,-\varepsilon_1).
\tag{26}
\]
Their coordinate distance is
\[
 \omega-\varepsilon_1
 =\frac{\rho H}{\rho+y}
 =\ell_2.
\]
The \(Q_1\)-triangle has transverse height \(\rho\), so
\[
 |Q_1|_\tau
 =\frac{\rho\ell_2}{2}
 =\frac{\rho^2H}{2(\rho+y)}.
\tag{27}
\]
Likewise, the line \(\tau_1=0\) cuts
\([y_2,y_3]\) at
\[
 b_2=(0,1+\varepsilon_2,-\varepsilon_2),
\tag{28}
\]
and
\[
 |Q_2|_\tau
 =\frac{\chi\ell_1}{2}
 =\frac{\chi^2H}{2(\chi+x)}.
\tag{29}
\]

The \(\tau_3=0\) section is parallel to the base.  The upper
\(Q_{123}\)-triangle is homothetic to \(A_2\), about \(y_3\), with
linear ratio \(z/H\).  Hence
\[
 |Q_{123}|_\tau
 =\frac{RH}{2}\left(\frac zH\right)^2
 =\frac{Rz^2}{2H}.
\tag{30}
\]
Subtracting (27), (29), and (30) from (25), and multiplying all four
areas by \(s^2\), proves (14)--(15).  Positivity of the displayed
\(q_{12}\) expression was already established geometrically by the
open \(Q_{12}\)-region.

The formulas for \(A_0\) are independent of the new side slopes.  The
triangle \(\{r_i\geq-\alpha_i\}\) has linear scale
\(1+\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3\).  Cutting it by
\(r_3\leq\theta\) removes a similar corner triangle of linear scale
\(1+\alpha_1+\alpha_2-\theta\), proving (16).  Direct integration of
the three strips \(r_i\leq0\) gives (17).  Intersecting (10) with
\(r_i\geq0\) gives the vertex list in (18), and shoelace gives its
area \(p\).

The closures of \(Q_1,Q_2\) contain, respectively, the side points
\(b_1,b_2\).  Their other non-singleton vertices lie on the common
base and are nonextreme in the joint hull.  Thus, in the
\(\tau\)-plane,
\[
 C_\tau
 =\operatorname{conv}\{y_1,y_2,b_2,b_1\}.
\tag{31}
\]
The complementary triangle
\(\operatorname{conv}\{b_1,b_2,y_3\}\) has side ratios
\[
 \frac{y}{\rho+y},\qquad
 \frac{x}{\chi+x}
\]
from \(y_3\) along the two sides of \(A_2\).  Its area is therefore
\[
 \frac{RH}{2}
 \frac{xy}{(\rho+y)(\chi+x)}.
\]
Subtracting it from (25) gives
\[
 |C_\tau|
 =
 \frac{
 RH(\rho\chi+\rho x+\chi y)
 }{
 2(\rho+y)(\chi+x)
 }.
\tag{32}
\]
The area multiplier \(s^2\) proves (21).

We next compute the mixed area in rational coordinates.  For a
counterclockwise edge vector \(e=(\delta r_1,\delta r_2)\), put
\[
 N_e=(\delta r_2,-\delta r_1).
\]
Positive homogeneity of the support function turns the polygonal
mixed-area formula into
\[
 2V(P,C)=\sum_{e\subset\partial P}h_C(N_e).
\tag{33}
\]
For the cyclic vertex list in (18), the four nonunit outward normals
are
\[
 (0,-\theta),\quad(1,1),\quad(-\theta,0),\quad
 (-(1-\theta),-(1-\theta)).
\tag{34}
\]
They sum to zero, so the translation in (6) cancels from (33).  We
may replace \(C\) by \(-sC_\tau\).

On \(C_\tau\), the maximum first and second coordinates are
\[
 1+\rho+\omega,\qquad 1+\chi+\omega.
\]
The minimum third coordinate is \(-\omega\), while the maximum third
coordinate is
\[
 -\min\{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\}
 =-\varepsilon.
\]
The four support terms in the order (34) are therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &s\theta(1+\chi+\omega),\qquad
 -s(1+\varepsilon),\\
 &s\theta(1+\rho+\omega),\qquad
 s(1-\theta)(1+\omega).
\end{aligned}
\tag{35}
\]
Their sum is \(s(\omega-\varepsilon+\theta R)\), proving (22).

It remains to impose the actual lower-crossing condition.  For
\(i=1,2\), put
\[
 \Phi_i(t)=
 |A_0\cap\{f_i\leq t\}|
 +|A_2\cap\{f_i\leq-t\}|.
\tag{36}
\]
At \(t=L_i\), all relevant coordinate cuts meet relative interiors
of polygon edges.  Equality in either row of (8) merely makes two
different coordinate cuts coincide at one such edge point.  Thus both
functions are differentiable there.

For \(i=1\), increasing \(t=L_1+\eta\) moves the large-endpoint
threshold to \(r_1=\eta/\Delta\).  Its section at \(r_1=0\) has
length \(\theta+\alpha_3\).  The small-endpoint threshold becomes
\[
 \tau_1\geq\frac{\eta}{\Delta+2}
 =\frac{\eta}{\Delta s}.
\]
The \(\tau_1=0\) section joins the base point
\((0,1+\omega,-\omega)\) to \(b_2\), and hence has length
\(\ell_1\).  Including the \(s^2\) area multiplier gives
\[
 \Phi_1'(L_1+)
 =\frac{\theta+\alpha_3-s\ell_1}{\Delta}.
\tag{37}
\]
The identical calculation in row \(2\) gives
\[
 \Phi_2'(L_2+)
 =\frac{\theta+\alpha_3-s\ell_2}{\Delta}.
\tag{38}
\]

The actual lower-crossing definition is
\[
 L_i=\inf\{t:c_i+\Phi_i(t)<h\},
 \qquad
 c_i+\Phi_i(L_i)=h.
\]
It supplies values immediately to the right of \(L_i\) for which the
endpoint distribution is smaller than at \(L_i\).
Differentiability therefore makes both right derivatives nonpositive.
Equations (37)--(38) prove (23).

Finally, use only the first inequality in (23).  Equations (15),
(18), and (20) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac pm
 &<
 \frac{s\ell_1}{s^2RH/2}\\
 &=
 \frac{2\chi}{sR(\chi+x)}
 <
 \frac{2}{sR}
 <2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{39}
\]
The first strict inequality uses
\[
 p=\theta-\frac{\theta^2}{2}
 <\theta<\theta+\alpha_3\leq s\ell_1.
\]
On the other hand,
\[
 \beta-2=\frac{12\sqrt{21}-7}{50}>0,
\]
where the sign follows from \(144\cdot21=3024>49\).
Therefore (1) gives \(p/m>\beta>2\), contradicting (39).  The second
actual crossing gives the symmetric contradiction
\[
 \frac pm<
 \frac{2\rho}{sR(\rho+y)}<2.
\]
Thus the two independent transverse slopes do not produce a survivor.
The simultaneous equalities
\[
 \rho z=\omega y,\qquad\chi z=\omega x
\]
force
\[
 (x,y,z)=
 \frac{(\chi,\rho,\omega)}{\rho+\chi+\omega},
\]
which is exactly the coalesced boundary treated in accepted fact
`16b9eb59c6ee0306`.  Hence the present noncoalesced class is a genuine
extension, not a reparametrization of that accepted case.

An exact computational audit, not used as proof, checked every
piecewise polygon formula.  SageMath 10.8 was run with
`sage --nodotsage -c` and `Polyhedron(..., base_ring=QQ)` at
\[
 \rho=\frac15,\quad\chi=\frac13,\quad\omega=\frac12,\quad
 (x,y,z)=\left(\frac25,\frac25,\frac15\right),\quad
 s=\frac32,\quad\theta=\frac14.
\]
The two strict side-order slacks were \(4/25\) and \(2/15\).  Exact
clipping returned
\[
 |A_2|_\tau=\frac{427}{600},
\]
\[
 (|Q_1|_\tau,|Q_2|_\tau,|Q_{12}|_\tau,|Q_{123}|_\tau)
 =
 \left(
 \frac7{300},\frac7{132},\frac{8889}{15400},\frac{61}{1050}
 \right),
\]
\[
 (\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\ell_1,\ell_2)
 =
 \left(\frac4{15},\frac2{11},\frac7{22},\frac7{30}\right),
\qquad
 |C_\tau|=\frac{2989}{6600}.
\]
Both the support sum and the independent Minkowski-sum calculation
gave
\[
 2V(P,C)=\frac{1091}{880}.
\]
An unequal-offset audit at
\((\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,\theta)
=(1/20,1/30,1/40,1/4)\) returned
\[
 M=\frac{2563}{9600},\qquad
 (u_1,u_2,u_3)
 =\left(\frac{11}{800},\frac{11}{1200},\frac{263}{9600}\right),
\]
exactly as in (16)--(17), and printed
`A0_ASSERTIONS_PASSED`.
The command asserted all displayed identities over `QQ`, printed
`ALL_ASSERTIONS_PASSED`, and exited with status \(0\).
Swapping \(\rho\) and \(\chi\) audited the other branch of the
minimum in (19): it returned
\((\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)=(2/11,4/15)\), again gave
\(2V(P,C)=1091/880\), printed
`SECOND_BRANCH_ASSERTIONS_PASSED`, and exited with status \(0\).
A third exact run used
\((x,y,z)=(18/25,2/25,1/5)\), for which
\((\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)=(0,22/79)\).  It gave
\(2V(P,C)=121/80\), printed
`ONE_COALESCED_ASSERTIONS_PASSED`, and exited with status \(0\).

WolframScript 1.13.0, invoked with the exact command prefix
```
wolframscript -local /Applications/Wolfram.app/Contents/MacOS/WolframKernel -code
```
The local Wolfram 14.3 kernel then performed the exact real elimination
```
Reduce[
 0 < theta < 1 && alpha3 > 0 && s > 1 && R > 1 &&
 H > 0 && chi > 0 && x > 0 &&
 p == theta - theta^2/2 &&
 m == s^2 R H/2 &&
 theta + alpha3 <= s chi H/(chi + x) &&
 p > 2 m,
 {theta, alpha3, s, R, H, chi, x, p, m}, Reals]
```
and returned `False` with exit status \(0\).  Four separate exact
`Together`/`Expand` checks returned residuals `{0,0,0,0}` for the two
identities in (20), the support sum (35), and the area subtraction
(32).  Replacing `p > 2 m` by
`p/m > (93 + 12 Sqrt[21])/50` in the exact `Reduce` query also
returned `False`.  An exact algebraic check returned
`BETA_GT_2=True`.  No floating infeasibility conclusion is used.
statement:
Assume all hypotheses and notation of accepted fact
`904839a1c6967954`.  Thus the full canonical single-double hypotheses
hold, including all three actual lower crossings, all three crossing
equalities, both tails, finite interior, compatibility, \(W=0\), and
\[
 \frac pm>\beta:=\frac{93+12\sqrt{21}}{50}>2,
 \qquad
 \Delta=-1-(L_1+L_2+L_3)>2.
\tag{1}
\]

Restrict to the following rational class.  After a common affine
change of the plane and a common area normalization, assume
\[
 L_1=L_2=L_3=-\frac{\Delta+1}{3},
 \qquad
 s:=\frac{\Delta+2}{\Delta}=1+\frac2\Delta.
\tag{2}
\]
Use coordinates
\[
 r_i=\frac{f_i-L_i}{\Delta},
 \qquad r_1+r_2+r_3=1,
\tag{3}
\]
and, on the smaller endpoint, the equivalent coordinates
\[
 \tau_i=-\frac{f_i+L_i}{\Delta+2},
 \qquad \tau_1+\tau_2+\tau_3=1.
\tag{4}
\]
Then
\[
 f_i\leq L_i\iff r_i\leq0,\qquad
 f_i\leq-L_i\iff\tau_i\geq0,
\tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 r_i=\frac{2(\Delta+1)}{3\Delta}-s\tau_i.
\tag{6}
\]

Let
\[
 \alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,\theta,\rho,\chi,\omega,x,y,z
 \in\mathbb Q
\]
satisfy
\[
 \alpha_i>0,\quad 0<\theta<1,\quad
 \rho,\chi,\omega,x,y,z>0,\quad x+y+z=1,
\tag{7}
\]
and the side-order conditions
\[
 \rho z\leq\omega y,\qquad
 \chi z\leq\omega x,
\tag{8}
\]
with at least one inequality strict.
Put
\[
 R=1+\rho+\chi+\omega,\qquad H=\omega+z.
\tag{9}
\]
Let the larger endpoint be the separator-normal trapezoid
\[
 A_0=
 \left\{
 r_1+r_2+r_3=1:
 r_i\geq-\alpha_i\ (i=1,2,3),\
 r_3\leq\theta
 \right\}.
\tag{10}
\]
In the \(\tau\)-plane let the smaller endpoint be the triangle
\[
 A_2=\operatorname{conv}\{y_1,y_2,y_3\},
\tag{11}
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
 y_1&=(1+\rho+\omega,-\rho,-\omega),\\
 y_2&=(-\chi,1+\chi+\omega,-\omega),\\
 y_3&=(x,y,z).
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
Let \(K\) be any rational two-dimensional convex polytope satisfying
all the inherited canonical hypotheses.  Then no such
\(A_0,A_2,K\) exist.

For completeness, every endpoint quantity in the conclusion has the
following exact formula.  The positive \(Q\)-support is precisely
\[
 \{J:q_J>0\}=\{123,1,2,12\},
\tag{13}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 q_1&=
 \frac{s^2\rho^2H}{2(\rho+y)},\\
 q_2&=
 \frac{s^2\chi^2H}{2(\chi+x)},\\
 q_{123}&=
 \frac{s^2Rz^2}{2H},\\
 q_{12}&=
 \frac{s^2}{2}\left(
 RH-\frac{\rho^2H}{\rho+y}
 -\frac{\chi^2H}{\chi+x}
 -\frac{Rz^2}{H}
 \right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
All four quantities in (14) are positive, and
\[
 m=|A_2|=\frac{s^2RH}{2}.
\tag{15}
\]

The large-endpoint area, its three lower-cap areas, and its empty-cell
area are
\[
 M=
 \frac{
 (1+\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3)^2
 -(1+\alpha_1+\alpha_2-\theta)^2
 }2,
\tag{16}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
 u_1&=\alpha_1(\theta+\alpha_3),\\
 u_2&=\alpha_2(\theta+\alpha_3),\\
 u_3&=\alpha_3(1+\alpha_1+\alpha_2)
 +\frac{\alpha_3^2}{2},
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
\[
 P=\overline{P_\varnothing}
 =\operatorname{conv}
 \{(1-\theta,0),(1,0),(0,1),(0,1-\theta)\},
\qquad
 p=\theta-\frac{\theta^2}{2}.
\tag{18}
\]

Define the two nonnegative side clearances and the two positive
coordinate-chord
lengths by
\[
 \varepsilon_1=
 \frac{\omega y-\rho z}{\rho+y},
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_2=
 \frac{\omega x-\chi z}{\chi+x},
 \qquad
 \varepsilon=\min\{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\},
\tag{19}
\]
\[
 \ell_1=
 \frac{\chi H}{\chi+x}
 =\omega-\varepsilon_2,
 \qquad
 \ell_2=
 \frac{\rho H}{\rho+y}
 =\omega-\varepsilon_1.
\tag{20}
\]
Then \(C\) is a rational quadrilateral with
\[
 |C|=
 \frac{
 s^2RH(\rho\chi+\rho x+\chi y)
 }{
 2(\rho+y)(\chi+x)
 },
\tag{21}
\]
and its exact mixed area with \(P\) is
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 2V(P,C)=s\bigl(\omega-\varepsilon+\theta R\bigr).
 \quad}
\tag{22}
\]
Finally, the first two actual lower crossings necessarily satisfy
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \theta+\alpha_3\leq s\ell_1,
 \qquad
 \theta+\alpha_3\leq s\ell_2.
 \quad}
\tag{23}
\]
